accepted.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee submitted its report in August 1978 with how many recommendations?
accepted.x: The Committee submitted its report in August 1978 and made 132 recommendations.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail to separate the committee from other Panchayati Raj committees.
accepted.sec: ■ Ashok Mehta Committee - government, PM, year, tiers, term  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Ashok Mehta Committee, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj structure.
2. It proposed a four-year term for the Panchayati Raj bodies.
3. It retained the three-tier structure without modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Committee proposed replacing the three-tier structure with a two-tier system and recommended a four-year term. It did not retain the three-tier structure unchanged.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the principal structural recommendation.
accepted.sec: ■ Ashok Mehta Committee - government, PM, year, tiers, term  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the two tiers proposed by the Ashok Mehta Committee?
accepted.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended Mandal Panchayats at the lower level and Zila Parishads at the district level.
accepted.tq: Match the recommended two-tier structure with the correct institutional names.
accepted.sec: ■ Ashok Mehta Committee - government, PM, year, tiers, term  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists:
List-I
(a) Zila Parishad
(b) Mandal Panchayat
(c) Ashok Mehta Committee report
(d) Ashok Mehta Committee appointment

List-II
(i) December 1977
(ii) Group of villages
(iii) August 1978
(iv) District-level executive body

Codes:
(a) (b) (c) (d)
accepted.x: The Zila Parishad was the district-level executive body; the Mandal Panchayat covered a group of villages; the report came in August 1978; and the committee was appointed in December 1977.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure institutional pair and then fix the dates.
accepted.sec: ■ Ashok Mehta Committee - government, PM, year, tiers, term  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Mandal Panchayat proposed by the Ashok Mehta Committee was intended to cover a population of approximately:
accepted.x: The proposed Mandal Panchayat was to comprise a group of villages with a population of about 15,000 to 20,000.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the population range of the lower tier from nearby plausible ranges.
accepted.sec: ■ Ashok Mehta Committee - government, PM, year, tiers, term  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Ashok Mehta Committee's scheme, which institution was regarded as responsible for district planning?
accepted.x: The Zila Parishad was envisaged as the district-level executive body responsible for district planning.
accepted.tq: Identify the body linked with the specific function of district planning.
accepted.sec: ■ Ashok Mehta Committee - government, PM, year, tiers, term  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Why did the Ashok Mehta Committee recommend compulsory taxation powers for Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: To transfer all Union taxes to local bodies
To impose taxes without legislative authority
To enable them to raise their own financial resources
To abolish grants from the State governments
accepted.x: Compulsory taxation powers were recommended so that Panchayati Raj Institutions could raise their own money and become financially capable.
accepted.tq: Link the recommended power with its stated institutional purpose.
accepted.sec: ■ Constitutional status, nyaya panchayats, taxation, social audit  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee envisaged regular social audit by:
o: A district-level agency and a committee of legislators
The Gram Sabha and the Supreme Court jointly
accepted.x: The Committee proposed regular social audit by a district-level agency together with a committee of legislators.
accepted.tq: Identify the combination of bodies assigned the audit function.
accepted.sec: ■ Constitutional status, nyaya panchayats, taxation, social audit  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the Ashok Mehta Committee, the first point of decentralisation below the State level was to be the:
accepted.x: The Committee treated the district as the first point of decentralisation under popular supervision below the State level.
accepted.tq: Separate the district-based recommendation from the commonly associated block-level structure.
accepted.sec: ■ Unit of decentralisation, lower tier, political parties, elections  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relationship between the lower and upper tiers under the Ashok Mehta scheme?
o: Taxation functions were to be transferred to the State Election Commission
Development functions and staff were to be transferred to the Zila Parishad
Judicial functions were to be transferred to the Zila Parishad
Development functions and staff were to be transferred to the Mandal Panchayat
accepted.x: The Committee recommended that development functions and staff should be transferred to the Zila Parishad, while the Mandal Panchayat was the lower tier.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of transfer rather than merely identifying the two tiers.
accepted.sec: ■ Unit of decentralisation, lower tier, political parties, elections  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended official participation of political parties in Panchayati Raj elections at:
accepted.x: The Committee recommended official participation of political parties at all levels of Panchayat elections.
accepted.tq: Watch for the scope word “all” when testing the extent of participation.
accepted.sec: ■ Unit of decentralisation, lower tier, political parties, elections  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: If a Panchayati Raj body was superseded under the Ashok Mehta Committee's recommendation, elections were to be held within:
accepted.x: The Committee recommended that elections should be conducted within six months if a Panchayati Raj body was superseded.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the prescribed election deadline from other common constitutional time limits.
accepted.sec: ■ Unit of decentralisation, lower tier, political parties, elections  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Ashok Mehta Committee?
1. State cabinet — Minister for Panchayati Raj
2. Panchayat elections — Chief Electoral Officer with the Chief Election Commissioner
3. Reservation — SC/ST representation according to population
accepted.x: The Committee recommended a Minister for Panchayati Raj in the State cabinet, election management involving the State's Chief Electoral Officer and the Chief Election Commissioner, and SC/ST reservation according to population.
accepted.tq: Verify each institutional recommendation before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: ■ Unit of decentralisation, lower tier, political parties, elections  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The principal political reason for the failure to implement the Ashok Mehta Committee recommendations was that:
o: The Supreme Court declared the recommendations unconstitutional
The Janata government fell before completing its term
The Planning Commission rejected the report immediately
The State governments unanimously implemented an alternative model
accepted.x: The Janata government fell before completing its term, and consequently the Centre took no action on the recommendations.
accepted.tq: Connect policy non-implementation with the political fate of the sponsoring government.
accepted.sec: ■ Fate of the recommendations - political reasons  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Panchayats formed after 1977 broadly on the lines suggested by the Ashok Mehta Committee are known as:
accepted.x: Panchayats formed after 1977 on the lines of the Ashok Mehta recommendations are referred to as Second Generation Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the generation label and descriptive institutional terms.
accepted.sec: ■ Fate of the recommendations - political reasons  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out with reference to committees that inquired into Panchayati Raj Institutions?
accepted.x: Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao were associated with Panchayati Raj inquiries. Dinesh Goswami was associated with electoral reforms.
accepted.tq: Group the committees by subject and identify the electoral-reforms committee.
accepted.sec: ■ Odd one out - PR vs other committees  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Administrative Reforms Commissions were associated with administrative reforms. Tarkunde and Dinesh Goswami were linked with electoral reforms, Sarkaria with Centre-State relations, and C. Rangarajan with the National Statistical Commission.
accepted.tq: Use the subject-area association to eliminate swapped committee functions.
accepted.sec: ■ Odd one out - PR vs other committees  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The V.R. Rao Committee of 1960 is associated with:
accepted.x: Although its name may suggest a statistical body outside the Panchayati Raj field, the V.R. Rao Committee was associated with Panchayat Statistics and was a Panchayati Raj committee.
accepted.tq: Resolve the look-alike committee trap by recalling its specific Panchayat-related subject.
accepted.sec: ■ Odd one out - PR vs other committees  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was set up in 1985 by the:
accepted.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was set up in 1985 by the Planning Commission to review administrative arrangements for rural development and poverty alleviation.
accepted.tq: Identify the appointing body before considering the committee's recommendations.
accepted.sec: ■ G.V.K. Rao Committee - appointing body, year, district-level recommendations  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee found that rural development administration had become:
o: Bureaucratised and cut off from Panchayati Raj Institutions
Decentralised and fully integrated with Panchayati Raj Institutions
accepted.x: The Committee observed that development administration had become bureaucratised and disconnected from Panchayati Raj Institutions, describing PRIs as “grass without roots.”
accepted.tq: Test the committee's diagnosis rather than its structural recommendations.
accepted.sec: ■ G.V.K. Rao Committee - appointing body, year, district-level recommendations  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the G.V.K. Rao Committee:
1. It regarded the Zila Parishad as an institution of pivotal importance.
2. It treated the district as the basic unit of planning.
3. It recommended that a District Development Commissioner should act as the Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the G.V.K. Rao Committee's district-level recommendations.
accepted.tq: Combine the committee's institutional, territorial and administrative recommendations.
accepted.sec: ■ G.V.K. Rao Committee - appointing body, year, district-level recommendations  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The District Development Commissioner recommended by the G.V.K. Rao Committee was to be in charge of:
accepted.x: The District Development Commissioner was proposed as the Zila Parishad's Chief Executive Officer and was to be in charge of all district development departments.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative office with the full extent of its proposed responsibility.
accepted.sec: ■ G.V.K. Rao Committee - appointing body, year, district-level recommendations  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the G.V.K. Rao Committee from the L.M. Singhvi Committee?
o: G.V.K. Rao focused on Gram Sabhas, while L.M. Singhvi focused on district bureaucracy
G.V.K. Rao focused on administrative arrangements, while L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising PRIs for democracy
G.V.K. Rao focused on constitutional recognition, while L.M. Singhvi focused on taxation powers
Both committees had identical objectives and key units
accepted.x: G.V.K. Rao examined the administrative set-up for rural development, whereas L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising Panchayati Raj Institutions as instruments of democracy.
accepted.tq: Separate committees by focus rather than by their common connection with Panchayati Raj.
accepted.sec: ■ G.V.K. Rao Committee - appointing body, year, district-level recommendations  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was recommended by the Thungon sub-committee in 1988?
o: Replacement of the State Finance Commission by the Union Finance Commission
A fixed five-year term for Panchayati Raj Institutions
accepted.x: The Thungon sub-committee recommended constitutional recognition, three tiers, a fixed five-year term and several other institutional safeguards, including a State Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Select a specific recommendation from a cluster of constitutional-status proposals.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Thungon sub-committee's recommendations, the maximum period for which a Panchayati Raj body could be superseded was:
accepted.x: The Thungon sub-committee proposed that supersession of a Panchayati Raj body should not exceed six months.
accepted.tq: Focus on the precise upper limit rather than the general recommendation of regular elections.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was specifically associated with the Thungon sub-committee's recommendations?
o: A constitutional list of subjects for Panchayati Raj Institutions, later reflected in the Eleventh Schedule
Direct elections only at the village level
Transfer of Panchayat taxation to the Election Commission
accepted.x: Thungon recommended placing a list of Panchayati Raj subjects in the Constitution; this was later reflected in the Eleventh Schedule.
accepted.tq: Connect the committee recommendation with its later constitutional institutionalisation.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Gadgil Committee of 1988 was set up by the:
accepted.x: The Gadgil Committee was set up by the Congress party in 1988 and its recommendations fed into the draft constitutional amendment proposals.
accepted.tq: Identify the political origin of the committee instead of confusing it with a governmental commission.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gadgil Committee:
1. It recommended direct elections at all three levels of Panchayati Raj.
2. It recommended a State Election Commission.
3. It recommended taxation powers for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Gadgil Committee recommended direct elections at all three levels, a State Election Commission and taxation powers for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Check whether each institutional safeguard belongs to the same committee before choosing the combined option.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G.V.K. Rao — Direct elections at all three levels
Thungon — Collector as Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad
accepted.x: Direct elections at all three levels were associated with the Gadgil recommendations. G.V.K. Rao focused on administrative arrangements, district planning and the District Development Commissioner.
accepted.tq: Find the committee whose central administrative focus does not fit the electoral recommendation.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
The recommendations of the Thungon and Gadgil committees shared which of the following features?
1. Constitutional recognition of Panchayati Raj Institutions
2. A three-tier structure
3. A five-year term
4. State-level financial arrangements for Panchayati Raj Institutions
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Both sets of recommendations supported constitutional recognition, a three-tier structure, a five-year term and State-level financial arrangements such as a State Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Identify common features across two committees rather than committee-specific additions.
accepted.sec: ■ Thungon and Gadgil - recommendations on constitutional status  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The opposition to constitutional amendment proposals concerning Panchayati Raj Institutions primarily argued that they would:
o: Centralise local governance by allowing the Centre to deal directly with local bodies over the States
Strengthen the exclusive legislative power of the States over local government
Eliminate all forms of local self-government
Transfer local government entirely to the judiciary
accepted.x: Critics argued that the proposals were centralising because they could enable the Centre to deal directly with local bodies over the heads of the States.
accepted.tq: Apply the federalism objection to the proposed Centre–local body relationship.
accepted.sec: ■ Opposition criticism - states' objections  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the constitutional distribution of legislative subjects, ‘Local Government’ is included in the:
accepted.x: Local Government is a subject in the State List, which formed the basis of the States' objection to greater direct Central involvement with local bodies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the federal list containing local government from the Union and Concurrent Lists.
accepted.sec: ■ Opposition criticism - states' objections  [GROUP-II]
